title: Step by step procedures: Degradation of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons in potable water using photo-Fenton oxidation process
author: Abd Manan, Beddu, et al.

steps.title: Prepare PAH solution and reagents
steps.instruction: Dissolve 17 USEPA‑PAHs in potable water to a concentration of 4 μg L⁻¹ (actual pH 6.96). Prepare 0.0075 M hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) and 0.00075 M ferrous sulfate (FeSO₄) stock solutions. Keep all solutions at room temperature (27 °C).

steps.title: Set up reactor and operating conditions
steps.instruction: Assemble the batch reactor (Fig. 1) equipped with a magnetic stirrer set to 300 rpm, a UV lamp EA‑160/FE (230 V, 0.17 A, 365 nm emission), and a thermometer. Verify the UV lamp is powered and the temperature is 27 °C. Use a HACH® portable pH meter to monitor pH.

steps.title: Run photo‑Fenton reaction and sample over time
steps.instruction: Add the prepared H₂O₂ and FeSO₄ solutions to the PAH‑containing water to achieve the target molarities. Start UV irradiation and magnetic stirring to ensure homogeneity. Conduct experiments at neutral pH (6.96) first, then repeat at acidic and alkaline pH as desired, keeping Fe concentration ≤ 1 mg L⁻¹ after each batch. Record reaction times and collect samples at the predetermined time points.

steps.title: Collect aliquots for COD and TOC analysis
steps.instruction: At each sampling time withdraw two aliquots: 2 mL for chemical oxygen demand (COD) determination and 20 mL for total organic carbon (TOC) measurement. For the COD aliquot, adjust the pH to > 10 by adding a few drops of NaOH to decompose residual H₂O₂ and minimise interference.

steps.title: Measure COD and TOC concentrations
steps.instruction: Determine COD using a HACH DR5000 spectrophotometer according to standard methods. Measure TOC with a Shimadzu TOC analyzer, using the 20 mL sample volume required by the instrument.

steps.title: Extract PAHs by solid‑phase extraction
steps.instruction: Condition a HyperSep Retain PEP column (60 mg, 3 mL, product code 10505905) and a C18 cartridge (Bond Elut C18, 500 mg, 6 mL, product code 12102052) sequentially with 10 mL DCM/n‑hexane (1:3 v/v), 10 mL methanol, and 10 mL ultrapure water. Load 500 mL of the water sample onto the cartridge at 5.0 mL min⁻¹. After loading, keep the cartridge under vacuum for 30 min to remove residual water.

steps.title: Concentrate extracts and prepare for GC‑MS
steps.instruction: Elute retained PAHs with 15 mL DCM/n‑hexane (1:3 v/v) at a flow rate of 1 mL min⁻¹. Evaporate the eluate to dryness using a Thermo Fisher Reacti‑Vap™ Evaporator (9‑port, product code TS‑18825) under a gentle nitrogen stream at room temperature. Re‑dissolve the residue in 1 mL DCM:n‑hexane (1:3 v/v) and transfer the solution into 1.5 mL septum‑capped vials. Store samples and analyse by GC‑MS within 40 days.

steps.title: Calibrate GC‑MS and analyze samples
steps.instruction: Prepare calibration standards of each of the 17 USEPA‑PAHs at 1 μg L⁻¹, 2 μg L⁻¹ and 3 μg L⁻¹. Inject standards into the GC‑MS, construct calibration curves (response vs. concentration) and verify that each curve has a correlation coefficient (R²) greater than 0.95. Run the prepared sample vials under the same GC‑MS conditions and quantify PAH concentrations before and after treatment.
